_about: HOME BASE (rule 437(b), rule 347, rule 343; ask lines 356 and 522): YOUR settlement, the one you plant. Read by engine/bohemia_home.js, which the map (slices/BOHEMIA_CITY_WORLD.html __HOME_BASE__) and the town screen read. A modder's file: every word is draft:true (WORDS overwrites), every number is a default HOME BASE set and TUNING owns (rule 38g: no felt number outside the table; this file is the table's row until TUNING folds it in). Realism first: a real settlement lives or dies by WATER, a ROAD, POWER and how near the raiders roam (the coordinator's 11/3 defaults, records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_THE_SETTLEMENT_YOU_PLANT_11_3_26.md).

grade._about: THE SMART SYSTEM (his 'maybe it'll be a smart system'): every block he stands on is graded on four marks, 0 to 3, by how near the nearest block of each kind is (within near[0] blocks a 3, within near[1] a 2, within near[2] a 1, else 0). DANGER reads the other way: 3 is a rival's home or a crew right on top of you. A block is a map cell (om.at), about a quarter mile.

danger._about: the nearest other faction's home base or roaming crew

needs._about: nothing is planted where no water reaches or no road comes in: the people die or nothing trades

grade._first_day_about: never in the first minute (the second votes, 9/23: nothing forced): the PLANT button is offered from the second day of a game

bill._about: YOU RUN IT, SO YOU PAY FOR IT (347(d)): taken at nightfall beside the crew's own bill. keep = the place's own lamp, gate and pump; each person who lives there eats and drinks what a crewman does (per_man_per_night is READ from records/target/bb/nightly_bill.json, never typed here); far water costs more (the vendor's premium, ECONOMY Day 47: water carried in costs a multiple of the pipe).
bill._prize_pays_about: a boss's prize standing at home pays back a day: THE POT's kitchen feeds one, THE TAP's main and THE FILTER's purifier water one (343(b)); counted as batteries off the bill, one each

plan._about: THE PLACE'S OWN GROUND, in house tiles (a combat tile is a house, 9/4), top-down: R a road, L a lot, the front row is the street the map's road comes in on. EVERY LOT FRONTS A ROAD and THE ROADS ARE ONE NETWORK (rule 429(h)); gates/home_base_gate.js fails a lot cut off or a stub split from the rest. Lots open as the place grows: 'open' lots at planting, then 'grow' more each time every open lot has something standing (progress you can see, 347(g)).

prizes._about: A BOSS'S PRIZE STANDS IN YOUR SETTLEMENT (343(b)): read from BohemiaBosses' own state (the verb his kill handed you); the piece is records/target/bb/home_lots.json's, never retyped here

residents._about: THE JOURNEY'S PEOPLE POST UP THERE (347(e)): once a place is planted, a man who leaves the company (let go, or walked when the batteries ran out) goes to live there instead of vanishing, with his face and his name; a spared boss (BOSSES' negotiable ones) and the retinue join the same list when those lanes call add(). Each one eats from the place's bill.

names._about: the place's name until he types his own (draft:true, WORDS); the player does not speak Spanglish, a place's name may

story._about: THE PLACE REMEMBERS (rule 412: 'a lot of your relations and experience with the settlements and your custom settlement will be remembered... they'll tell a story about your granddad'). Every planting, move-in, finished build, prize and name is kept on the place's record; a person who lives there tells it from his own mouth and face (rule 9/20), 'you' in the act it happened, 'your father' one act on, 'your granddad' two on. Words draft:true, WORDS overwrites; the player does not speak Spanglish, the people who live there may.

builds._about: WHAT HE BUILDS AT HIS PLACE AND WHY IT MATTERS (rule 343: it changes because of him; rule 441: whole). Every build at his place costs the one battery and the day engine/bohemia_lotbuild.js already charges PLUS the goods below out of the company's supplies (the top bar's own counts, bohemia.supplies.v1), and every morning it stands it puts what it gives into those same supplies, so the top bar moves; a person who lives there works one build each, in lot order, and a worked build gives its 'worked' more. MEASURED FIRST (11/10, the demo): the garden, the tank, the pump and the shed paid one 'resources' a day, a purse currency no screen shows, while their lines said '+1 food/day', '+1 water/day', '+1 tape/day'. Food and water are one count (rule 209). Every number a default HOME BASE set, TUNING's to change; words draft:true.

opens._about: WHAT YOU BUILD OPENS A DOOR (HOME BASE 11/11, rule 445(b) it starts bare and grows by what he does, rule 343): at his planted place a door that does something stays SHUT until the build that houses it stands, and its sheet says what opens it (rule 438: no door does nothing in silence). Every other town's door is untouched. Words draft:true (WORDS overwrites); the player does not speak Spanglish.

grinder.name: GRINDER
grinder._about: HOME BASE 3 11/22 (VAMILY rule 469, rule 456(b)): one at his place, beside the forge; the dead his company brings home go in, the head first out; one tap, the sausage is in the top bar's FOOD. Its picture is the 11/3 pipeline's own piece (records/target/home_settlement/ pieces grinder_*, tools/bohemia_home_base_his_pieces_11_21_26.py grinder). Every rule under it is the grinder block below.

THE GRINDER (HOME BASE 3, 11/22; VAMILY rule 469, his 'C' and 'Ppl dont eat the brain tho'; rules 456, 460, 455, 466(c)). Read by engine/bohemia_grinder.js through the map (slices/BOHEMIA_CITY_WORLD.html __THE_GRINDER__) and the town screen (slices/BOHEMIA_SETTLEMENT_SCREEN.html __THE_GRINDER__). One tap on screen; everything else here runs underneath and is never explained (466(c)). Every number a default HOME BASE set, realism first, TUNING's to move (rule 38g); 'ours' marks a number no record gives, a draft.

carry_a_man.unit: bodies a man of the company carries home from a won fight (the room is kilos: men x this x body_kg)
carry_a_man.source: a litter over a long walk wants four bearers taking turns, two at a time (US Army FM 4-25.11 First Aid, litter carries); an improvised drag on a tarp takes three. A starting crew of three brings one body; six bring two; twelve bring four. The rest are left where they fell.

body_kg.unit: kilos, a lean adult in a hungry valley
body_kg.source: the US adult mean is about 80 kg (CDC NHANES 2015-2018); a long famine takes a quarter of it (the Minnesota Starvation Experiment, Keys et al. 1950: 25% lost in 24 weeks); 80 x 0.775 = 62

meat_share.unit: of a body's weight that is boneless meat a hand strips for the grinder, after the head, the spine, the guts, the skin and the bones
meat_share.source: a hunter's boneless yield is about 27% of a deer's live weight (field dressed about 75% of live, boneless 35 to 40% of that: Penn State Extension, 'Venison: from field to table'); the ceiling is all an adult man's skeletal muscle, 24 of 66 kg (Cole 2017, Scientific Reports 7:44707)

cure_keep.unit: of the meat's weight that comes out as cured, smoked sausage (salt in, water out)
cure_keep.source: a smoked sausage loses about 10 to 20% in the smokehouse, a dry cure 30 to 40% (USDA FSIS, 'Sausages and Food Safety'); rule 460: salt decides it, the pool stores' 40-pound bags

kg_a_night.unit: kilos of sausage that are one man's night of food
kg_a_night.source: READ by the map from records/target/bb/carcass.json meat.kg_a_night when it is in (one number for meat in this game); this is the fallback

grinder.worked: one body: 62 x 0.27 x 0.8 = 13.4 kg = 26 nights of food; a crew of six (two bodies) brings home about four days' food for six, about 52 batteries at the counter's 2, against a routine contract's 30 (records/target/BOHEMIA_BOARD_SHELF.json)

keep_h.unit: game hours the dead keep on the road before they turn (thrown out at the grinder, said nowhere)
keep_h.source: above 32 C perishable food is unsafe after one hour (USDA FSIS danger zone); a gutted carcass in the desert night's cold and the day's shade lasts about a day, the hot-weather hunter's rule: on ice the same day (rule 460: raw meat here turns within an hour or two in the sun)

head_out.about: the head and the brain come off first and go in the lidded drum, never the grinder; everybody knows (Paolo 11/21: 'Ppl dont eat the brain tho'). The grinder's line says it, nothing else does.

bad_cut_pct.unit: percent of the batches with people in them that take a bad cut (the spine split, the cord or a piece of the brain in the grinder)
bad_cut_pct.source: ours, draft: a careful hand rarely gets it wrong. The real record: spinal cord got into mechanically separated beef often enough in the BSE years that it was banned from food (UK 1995, EU 2000, US FSIS 2004 for cattle over 30 months)

bought_bad_pct.unit: percent of the food bought at any stall in one tap that came from somebody who does not care (people, with the brain in)
bought_bad_pct.source: ours, draft: the 'batch bought from someone who does not care' (rule 469(b)); rare, and never said

takes_pct.unit: percent that a man's night eaten out of a bad batch gives him the shakes
takes_pct.source: ours, draft. The real record: kuru struck the Fore who ate the brain and the cord at the mortuary feasts (mostly women and children); muscle meat carries little to none (Alpers 2008, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 363:3707; Collinge et al. 2006, Lancet 367:2068)

incubation_years.unit: years from the bad night to the first tremor (drawn per man, a long right tail)
incubation_years.source: kuru's incubation runs 4.5 years to over 50, the mean about 12 (Collinge et al. 2006, Lancet 367:2068; Alpers 2008). The acts are 35 years apart (engine/bohemia_acts.js, draft), so in this game it shows in a later act: the family meets what the father ground.

dies_years.unit: years from the first tremor to death
dies_years.source: kuru kills in about twelve months, in three stages: walking, sitting, lying (Alpers 2008)

days_a_year.unit: game days in a year, for a mark that shows inside its own act

found_out_pct.unit: percent that a town finds out, on one sale of food with people in it, that it was people
found_out_pct.source: ours, draft. Legal nowhere and done everywhere (rule 469(c)): in the siege of Leningrad meat patties of people sold in the markets and the NKVD arrested about two thousand for it in 1941-42 (Bidlack and Lomagin, The Leningrad Blockade, 2012); buyers bought and did not ask, and a seller caught was finished there

found_out_act.source: records/target/bb/relations.json acts: the Battle Brothers Relations ladder's 'Minor Offensive Action -10' (bb_all/1670_Relations.txt), no new number invented

hungry_never_asks.about: a town whose stall is short of food (its need card is on) never finds out: a starving market does not ask what is in the meat (the famine record above)

shakes_town_act.source: records/target/bb/relations.json acts: 'Offensive Action -20'. A town he sold a bad batch to finds out when its own people shake, years on (the same incubation), once

look._about: HOME BASE 5 11/27, rule 347(c): what he changes at his place by tapping it (records/BOHEMIA_HOME_BASE_HIS_PLACE_HIS_WAY_THE_RESEARCH_11_27_26.md). A move and a paint cost nothing and take no time (Stardew Valley's Robin moves a building for nothing). paints: the first is bare (as built); 'hex' is the colour he picks by day, 'ir' how it reads on his night cameras (near-infrared: lime whitewash and red-oxide primer reflect it and glow, carbon-black tar soaks it up), a multiplier on the piece's light. Words draft:true (WORDS); TUNING's to move.

flow._about: YOUR PLACE IS EASY (HOME BASE 6 11/27, VAMILY rule 492(a)): the one next step, said by his crew's best man on the map's glass (slices/bohemia_your_place.js), each line short enough to read at a glance; engine/bohemia_home.js step() picks which. Every word draft:true (WORDS overwrites). {why} is the reason the ground he stands on is no good, {dir} the way to better ground.
